title: Left properness for simplicial categories with fixed objects
statement: Let $O$ be a small set and let $\mathrm{sCat}_O$ be the category of small simplicial categories with object set $O$ and enriched functors inducing the identity on $O$, with the model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. A weak equivalence in this model structure means a weak homotopy equivalence on every simplicial mapping set, and a cofibration means a map with the left lifting property against every objectwise trivial Kan fibration. This model structure is left proper: if $u:A\to B$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence and $i:A\to C$ is a cofibration in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, the canonical map $C\to B\amalg_A C$, where the pushout is in $\mathrm{sCat}_O$, is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. No mapping set of $A,B,C$ is required to be Kan.

source.place: Lemma 3.4, printed p. 11: properness of the fixed-object model SC_X, attributed there to Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Proposition 7.3. Only left properness is extracted here. No Stacks tag states this enriched-model result.

proof.text: Work throughout with the fixed set $O$. Write $*$ for coproduct with identities on $O$ amalgamated. Coproducts and pushouts of simplicial categories with this fixed set are computed degreewise in ordinary categories on $O$: a functor out of the degreewise colimit is a cocone in each degree, and compatibility with every simplicial operator follows by the colimit universal property. In particular the pushout exists by the model structure in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. That node also says a cofibration is a retract of a free simplicial extension. To ensure the retract fixes the domain, start with an arrow retract of $j_0:A_0\to C_0$: write its domain maps as $a:A\to A_0$, $b:A_0\to A$, and its codomain maps as $s_0:C\to C_0$, $r_0:C_0\to C$, with $ba=1_A$, $r_0s_0=1_C$, $j_0a=s_0i$, and $r_0j_0=ib$. Push $j_0$ out along $b$ and call the result $j:A\to\widetilde C$. In each degree $C_{0,q}=A_{0,q}*F_q$ gives $\widetilde C_q=A_q*F_q$ by the coproduct universal property, with the same chosen new generators. The composite of $s_0$ with $C_0\to\widetilde C$ is a section under $A$, because $ba=1_A$. The maps $i:A\to C$ and $r_0:C_0\to C$ induce its retraction by the pushout universal property, and their composite on $C$ is $r_0s_0=1_C$. Thus choose $A\xrightarrow{j}\widetilde C$ and maps $s:C\to\widetilde C$, $r:\widetilde C\to C$ under $A$ with $rs=1_C$, where in every degree $q$ one has $\widetilde C_q=A_q*F_q$ for an ordinary free category $F_q$. We first prove the conclusion for $j$, then take this retract. No fibrancy is used.

source.place: Sections 7.4–7.6; fixed-object pushouts and reduction to a strong free retract

proof.text:
First establish the coproduct invariance needed below directly from lower-level inputs, to avoid a cyclic dependency through coherent-nerve comparison. Let $v:X\to X'$ be a local weak equivalence and let $P$ be a constant free category on a graph $Q$ on $O$. For $x,y\in O$, every arrow in $X*P$ has a unique expression as graph edges $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ with one $X$-arrow before, between, and after them, allowing these $X$-arrows to be identities. To obtain it, split all free words into graph edges and compose each intervening block of $X$-arrows; relations in $X$ neither remove nor identify graph edges. Thus its mapping simplicial set is the disjoint union over such edge patterns of
$$X(x,s(e_1))\times X(t(e_1),s(e_2))\times\cdots\times X(t(e_t),y),$$
with $X(x,y)$ for $t=0$. This description is compatible with simplicial operators. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], realization preserves these disjoint unions and finite products in k-spaces. Path components and based homotopy groups of a finite product are the corresponding products, since maps and homotopies into a product are tuples of maps and homotopies. In a disjoint union each path and based sphere lies in its component. Consequently the product and disjoint-union maps induced by $v$ induce the bijections and group isomorphisms defining weak homotopy equivalence in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Hence $X*P\to X'*P$ is a local weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.7, proof (i), free-factor case; explicit word and realization argument

proof.text: If $P$ is instead a simplicial category free in every degree, form, for each $x,y$, the bisimplicial sets $D_{p,q}=(X_q*P_p)(x,y)$ and $D'_{p,q}=(X'_q*P_p)(x,y)$. The operators act on separate factors and commute by the coproduct universal property, even when faces of $P$ do not preserve its chosen generators. For fixed $p$, step 2 gives a weak equivalence in the $q$ direction. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. The diagonals are exactly $(X*P)(x,y)$ and $(X'*P)(x,y)$; their comparison is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.7, proof (ii), passage from a constant free factor to a degreewise free factor by diagonals

proof.text:
For an arbitrary simplicial category $Z$ on $O$, use the explicit free-category comonad $F$ in [lem-coef-free-resolution-coproduct-augmentation]. Put
$$E^X_{p,q}=(X_q*F^{p+1}Z_q)(x,y),\qquad T^X_{p,q}=(X_q*Z_q)(x,y),$$
with $T^X$ constant in $p$, and define the same objects for $X'$. For fixed $q$, the cited augmentation theorem applies to the ordinary categories $X_q,Z_q$, with no freeness hypothesis on either; it gives $E^X_{\bullet,q}\to T^X_{\bullet,q}$ a weak equivalence, and likewise for $X'$. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] both diagonal augmentations are weak equivalences. For fixed $p$, $q\mapsto F^{p+1}Z_q$ is degreewise free, so step 3 gives $E^X_{p,\bullet}\to E^{X'}_{p,\bullet}$ a weak equivalence. Applying the diagonal theorem again and two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] to the commuting augmentation square proves $X*Z\to X'*Z$ a local weak equivalence. Interchanging factors and composing proves that any finite coproduct of local weak equivalences in the fixed-object category is a local weak equivalence. This argument has not used left properness or the coherent-nerve comparison.

source.place: Propositions 2.6 and 2.7(iii), free resolutions and two diagonal comparisons

proof.text:
Return to a free extension $j:A\to\widetilde C$ and any map $v:A\to V$ on $O$. Define an augmented bisimplicial category by
$$R^V_{n,q}=\widetilde C_q*\underbrace{A_q*\cdots*A_q}_{n\text{ factors}}*V_q\quad(n\geq0),\qquad D^V=\widetilde C\amalg_A V.$$
The first face uses $j$ to send the first displayed $A$ factor into $\widetilde C$, each internal face folds adjacent $A$ factors, and the last face uses $v$ to send the last $A$ into $V$. Degeneracy $s_i$ inserts an unused $A$ factor in the corresponding position, by the unit map $I_O\to A$; here $I_O$ is the category with only identities, the coproduct unit. The augmentation sends each factor into the pushout. On any factor the simplicial identities say either that inserting and then deleting a position is the identity, or that two folds compose the same three inclusions. These are equal by associativity of composition and the coproduct universal property. The $q$ operators commute with these maps because $j,v$ are simplicial functors. This constructs the bisimplicial mapping sets and their augmentation to the diagram constant in $n$ on $D^V_q(x,y)$.

source.place: Section 8.2, coproduct bar for a pushout; operators and augmentation written explicitly

proof.text: Fix $q$. Apply [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-bar-reordering] to the free-extension bar of step 5: the factor braiding identifies its row with $R^V_{n,q}=F_q*A_{q,0}*\cdots*A_{q,n}*V_q$, and identifies every face, degeneracy and augmentation with the displayed labelled coproduct-bar operators. By [lem-coef-fixed-object-scat-pushout-coproduct], the augmentation target $(F_q*A_q)\amalg_{A_q}V_q$ is canonically $F_q*V_q$, with the stated structure map. Apply [lem-coef-split-coproduct-bar-extra-degeneracy] to $F_q,A_q,V_q,v_q$; its initial-factor insertion identities therefore hold on every mapping set in this row, including $d_1h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$.

source.place: Sections 7.4–7.6 and Proposition 8.2, printed p.279: fixed-object coproduct bar reordering, pushout identification, and initial-factor insertion.

proof.text: For every $q,x,y$, apply [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] to the row augmentation of step 6, with $S=(F_q*V_q)(x,y)$. It gives a simplicial section $s$ with $\varepsilon s=1$ and a simplicial cylinder homotopy $s\varepsilon\simeq1$. The other composite has the constant homotopy because it equals the identity. These are precisely the two homotopies required by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], applied to $u=\varepsilon$ and $v=s$. Therefore every row augmentation is a weak homotopy equivalence. Both cited statements allow empty simplicial sets and impose no Kan condition.

source.place: Section 8.2, explicit contraction of the split ordinary pushout row and diagonal argument

proof.text: The augmentation $R^V\to\operatorname{const}_nD^V$ constructed in step 5 is a morphism of bisimplicial mapping sets. Step 7 gives its weak equivalence in the $n$ direction for every fixed $q$. Apply the exchanged-direction assertion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to obtain the local weak equivalence $\varepsilon_V:\operatorname{diag}R^V\to D^V$. The factors $F_q$ and the contractions need not be natural in $q$: the diagonal theorem requires only the natural augmentation, already constructed in step 5, and the separate row weak equivalences.

source.place: Section 8.2, explicit contraction of the split ordinary pushout row and diagonal argument

proof.text: Apply steps 5–8 first to $V=A$, $v=1_A$, and then to $V=B$, $v=u$. In the first case $D^A=\widetilde C$, and in the second $D^B=\widetilde C\amalg_A B$. There is a map of augmented bars $R^A\to R^B$ that is the identity on $\widetilde C$ and every intermediate $A$ and is $u$ on the last factor. It commutes with the last face because that face uses $v$; it commutes with all other operators since they act on the unchanged factors. For fixed $n$, step 4 makes this finite-coproduct map a local weak equivalence of simplicial categories. The diagonal theorem [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] therefore gives a local weak equivalence on diagonals. Both vertical augmentations in the resulting commuting square are local weak equivalences by step 8. Its bottom arrow is precisely the canonical $\widetilde C\to\widetilde C\amalg_A B$, since on each factor the augmentation uses the pushout structure map. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] proves that bottom arrow is a local weak equivalence.

source.place: Sections 8.1–8.2 and 7.3(ii), comparing the identity span with the given weak-equivalence span

proof.text: Push out the maps $s,r$ of step 1 along $A\to B$. The pushout universal property gives maps $C\amalg_A B\to\widetilde C\amalg_A B\to C\amalg_A B$ whose composite is the identity, and the canonical arrows from $C,\widetilde C$ form commuting squares with them. Thus $C\to C\amalg_A B$ is a retract, in the arrow category, of the local weak equivalence of step 9. On every mapping set it is a retract of a weak homotopy equivalence. Weak equivalences are retract-closed in the simplicial-set model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], proving the required conclusion for $i$. For $O=\varnothing$ there are no mapping sets and the conclusion is vacuous. Empty mapping sets, loop generators, and identity-only categories are all allowed in the word and contraction constructions.

source.place: Sections 7.6 and 8.2, retract reduction and conclusion
